subject: honey buzzard
title: This Bird of Prey Raids Hornet Nests and Shrugs Off the Stings

scenes.text: One bird of prey hunts the thing everything else runs from.
The crested honey buzzard raids the nests of bees, wasps and hornets, while the whole colony swarms it.
It isn't there for honey. It tears out the comb to eat the larvae and pupae inside.
Its armor is on its face: short, dense feathers that overlap like scales around the eyes and beak.
Nearly five feet of wingspan, and it lives on grubs it steals from the angriest insects alive.

description:
The crested (Oriental) honey buzzard is a bird of prey that makes its living raiding the nests of bees, wasps and hornets.
It eats the combs, larvae and pupae while the colony attacks it. Its protection is in its feathers: the lores, the area between eye and beak that is bare in many raptors, are covered in short, dense, scale-like feathers, and fine filament-like structures around the eyes may help deter the insects. It also has long, narrow nostrils and longer claws on two toes that may help it dig out underground wasp nests. Its wingspan is 130 to 150 cm. Although it specialises in nests, it also takes other small prey.
Would you trade places with it for one meal? Comment below.
first_comment: A special membrane also protects its eyes during a raid. Would you trade places with it for one meal?
